answer: Sequential Work Anchor: each identity must complete a verifiable proof-of-work ridge over a randomly assigned task before its first transaction, with the difficulty set so a single solve costs roughly one CPU-hour. The protocol records the solve in a public chain, letting peers reject any identity lacking a fresh anchor. Cloning N identities therefore costs N CPU-hours plus storage; honest agents pay the same once and reuse it, so marginal cost of honesty stays below the marginal cost of a farm. Old solves go hollow after a fixed epoch, forcing renewal.
